legend: The Pontianak (Malay village folklore, Malaysia and Indonesia)
lines: Malaysia, a village at night, long ago.
A sweet scent of frangipani drifts between the houses.
The villagers know what it means, and they lock their doors.
Legend says the pontianak is near.
A woman in white, with black hair down to her knees.
She waits in the old banyan tree for lone travelers.
She calls out in a soft, sad voice, so you will come closer.
But the elders say a nail in the back of her neck makes her gentle.
Would you follow a sweet scent in the dark?
title: The Pontianak: The Sweet Smell That Means She Is Near #shorts
description:
In Malay folklore, the pontianak is a pale woman in white who waits in banyan trees. Legend says a sudden scent of frangipani means she is close.
